name: runtime-execution
description: Policy-neutral child-process execution primitives used by Revisor adapters, including captured output, timeout termination, platform launch shims (the Windows cmd.exe shim for npm CLIs and the opt-in WSL launch for the codex CLI), the Windows-native Codex sandbox-launch workaround, and per-call environment forwarding.
cardTemplate: Summarise the runtime-execution domain: policy-neutral child-process invocation, timeout ownership, captured output, and environment forwarding.
specRefs: SPEC-CODEX-SANDBOX-MODE: Windows native Codex sandbox launcher の回避
rationale: Security-scan policy owns the meaning and lifecycle of CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR. The generic process runner only forwards an optional environment and owns the spawned process lifecycle, so it remains reusable by CI and other adapters without importing review-gate policy. The WSL launch and Windows-native sandbox selections live here for the same reason as the cmd.exe shim: they answer "how is a CLI started on this host", not "what should be reviewed". Runtime defaults to native and sandboxing defaults to enabled; danger-full-access is restricted to the affected native Windows runtime.
